facts_used.why_it_matters: A +4.9% single session is the one genuinely one-day-scoped fact in the packet. With realised_vol_63_annual 0.7294 the daily sigma is roughly 4.6%, so this is only about a 1-sigma day and says little about the next close; it raises dispersion rather than establishing direction, and post-spike next-session behaviour is at best weakly positive.

A dated revision on the packet asof date is the only item that satisfies the rule-5 exception for a fresh dated analyst revision, and the standing results say revisions (unlike target levels) still carry information. It is same-day/reactive to the move, so it nudges rather than drives the call.
Positive revision breadth (44 net raises out of 70 revisions) means the analyst reaction function around this name is tilted upward, which mildly favours relative performance on a fresh-news day.

At 2.14 beta, most of a one-session relative return is SPY direction, which is UNKNOWN in the packet. This is the single largest force driving the outcome and it is unobservable here, which is why the estimate stays near 0.50 and the tails are wide.
Very high realised vol means the next-session relative return has a wide, low-signal distribution; a modest edge in expectation is mostly swamped by noise, so conviction must be capped.

Deeply extended above the 200-day (and vs_52w_high -0.0039, drawdown_63 0.0) means it is at highs with no recent drawdown; extension is not a one-day fact and is not treated as a predictor.

facts_used.why_it_matters: The decisive structural fact. Near-zero beta means the relative-return question collapses into almost a pure absolute-return bet on CRM's own idiosyncratic distribution; unlike a high-beta name, the unknown SPY direction barely enters. This is what justifies leaning on the name's own recent price action instead of parking at 0.50 by default.

An 8.7% five-session decline is the only genuinely recent extreme in the packet, and it is the one item with plausible one-day relevance: a sharp multi-day selloff can bounce the next close. It cuts both ways (oversold reflex vs falling-knife continuation), so it justifies a tilt, not a tail â€” and it is 5 sessions, not 1, so rule 5 bars using it to reach 0.30/0.70.

The asof session itself was only -0.63%, essentially flat. There is no single-session shock to extrapolate, and with realised_vol_63_annual 0.6131 (daily sigma ~3.9%) the last day is well under one sigma â€” i.e. no one-day event evidence.

It sits just before the selloff, implying analysts were constructive before the drop rather than after it.
